messages:
maria (AE): Heads up — AcmeBank POC kicked off. They sent an ISO questionnaire and want a short applicability statement covering POC scope, KMS (BYOK), and log retention. Need answers by EOD. cc @alex (SE) @june (Security)

alex (SE): Got it. Quick q: is this POC going to run on Redwood Dedicated or Private? Their email says 'customer VPC' but wanted to confirm.

maria (AE): They asked for Private (VPC) deployment for the POC — just 2 nodes, limited dataset (~500GB).

june (Security): Ok. For ISO applicability we normally say the ISMS covers Redwood control plane + the managed components we operate in the customer's VPC for the POC duration. Customer controls their VPC. Draft below.

june (Security): ```
ISMS Applicability (POC - AcmeBank):
- In-scope: Redwood Control Plane (identity, access management, centralized logging), POC-specific model serving instances deployed by Redwood into the customer's VPC (network policy endpoints we manage).
- Out-of-scope: Customer-managed resources inside their VPC (host hardening, customer third-party services), on-prem hardware, and customer operational processes.
- Cryptography: Data-at-rest encrypted using customer-managed keys (BYOK) — key lifecycle and rotation are customer responsibilities; Redwood holds limited, auditable access via least-privilege role.
- Retention: Operational logs retained for 30 days for the POC unless otherwise agreed; audit logs retained by default for 90 days (can be reduced for POC).
```

alex (SE): For evidence they asked for policy docs + network diagram. I can attach a simple diagram and pull the excerpt from our ISMS docs. Also need to confirm KMS integration steps — @june can you confirm BYOK for Private?

june (Security): Yes — we support BYOK in Private. Implementation note for the email: customer creates an AWS/GCP KMS key, grants Redwood a role `redwood-kms-decrypt` scoped to the POC timeframe. We record key usage in audit logs. Add line: "Key access is via least-privilege IAM role; key policies remain customer-controlled."

alex (SE): I'll include a short ops snippet for the presales docs: 
```
# kms_setup.sh (example)
aws kms create-key --description "Acme POC key"
# attach policy to allow arn:aws:iam::0123456789:role/redwood-kms-decrypt
```

maria (AE): They also asked whether having ISO certification is required to start the POC. How do we position that?

june (Security): We usually say: certification is not required to start a POC. We will provide a controls mapping and an evidence pack for the scope. If they require ISO 27001 certification for a production contract, we escalate to Dedicated/Private enterprise contract and provide cert details.

alex (SE): One more ops suggestion: mark ephemeral logs explicitly excluded from the POC scope (no persistent backups) unless the customer requests them — reduces evidence surface and complexity.

maria (AE): :thumbsup: I'll draft the reply with the applicability statement, network diagram, KMS steps, and ask if they want the full evidence pack or just the mapping. Target: EOD.

sre-bot: Deployed presales bundle to /shared/presales/acmebank/poc_1759009876.zip :package: (internal link)

june (Security): Added a note: default audit log retention for Private is 90 days; for the POC we can offer 30 days if they need a smaller window — include both options in the email.

maria (AE): Great — sending now. Thanks team!
